title: New Solubility Data of Hydrocarbons in Water and Modeling Concerning Vapor-Liquid-Liquid Binary Systems

verified_against_page_image.reason: HTML capture only, no PDF consulted

experimental_method: Static-analytic method with online Rolsi liquid/vapour samplers and GC (TCD+FID); VLLE conditions, 288 K up to below the hydrocarbon critical temperature.
uncertainties_stated: T +/-0.02 K; P +/-0.3 kPa; mole numbers +/-2% water, +/-2% ethane, +/-2.5% propane, +/-1.3% n-butane, +/-2% isobutane, +/-1.5% n-pentane, +/-1% n-hexane.

not_extracted_tables.Table 2: three-phase vapour pressures of ethane-water and propane-water: measured P3(T) but no solute composition; the pressures reappear in Tables 5-6 (calculated column and correlation not in scope)
not_extracted_tables.Table 3: three-phase vapour pressures of isobutane/n-butane/n-pentane-water: no composition, pressure only (same reason as Table 2)
not_extracted_tables.Table 12: parameters of the Henry constant correlation (fit)
not_extracted_tables.Table 13: parameters of the activity coefficient correlation (fit)

quality_remarks: Table 2 (not extracted) prints the ethane three-phase pressure as 3.4122 MPa at all four temperatures (288.33-303.30 K) while Table 5 gives 3.4122, 3.7883, 4.1982 and 4.6146 MPa at those temperatures; the constant column in Table 2 is probably a copy error.
Table 4 (not extracted) prints temperature ranges truncated (288-30, 298-34 etc.).

n-Butane (Table 8) rows at 313.24-353.14 K and n-pentane/n-hexane rows are non-monotonic in pressure (e.g. 0.5669 MPa at 303.31 K then 0.3868 MPa at 313.24 K) because the first two n-butane points and all pentane/hexane points use helium-adjusted pressure; the pressure is therefore not the saturation pressure for these rows.
Large rel dev (up to 8.9% n-butane, -9.7% n-pentane) between the authors' own correlation and the data: caused by the authors' fit, not by the table.
Abstract: minimum T 288 K (ethane 288.33 K), consistent. Maximum T below the hydrocarbon critical temperature consistent (ethane 303.30 K vs Tc 305.32 K).

Temperature scale not stated (Pt100 calibrated against a 25 ohm reference probe); the xexp unit scale (x10^3 ... x10^6) is read from the headers: ethane 10^3, propane 10^4, isobutane 10^4, n-butane 10^5, n-pentane 10^5, n-hexane 10^6.
extraction_notes: Header glyphs transliterated to ASCII (delta_x for the Greek delta x, 'x' for the multiplication sign); footnote letters stripped from header and cells into the note column; Unicode minus replaced by ASCII minus. Hydrocarbon gases other than the seven kept per SPEC v2.1 (i-c4h10, n-c4h10, n-c5h12, n-c6h14).
